successors.name: Carthage
successors.text: the western colonies: Sardinia, western Sicily, Malta and the Spanish coast

successors.name: kition
successors.text: Kition (Larnaca) on Cyprus, a Phoenician city-kingdom until Ptolemy I 'conquered Cyprus in 312 BC and killed Poumyathon, the Phoenician king of Kition'

ledger.x: Late 10th century BC: Tyre begins to plant colonies.
8th-7th century BC: the colonies of the western Mediterranean.
7th century BC: more Phoenician towns in Sardinia and Sicily.
7th century BC: the western Phoenician colonies pass to Carthage.

certainty.note: Trading stations and their hinterlands; no page gives a frontier, an area or a boundary for any colony, so the radius and the Cliopatria cells are drawn soft.
